lines.text: Do you know how a self-driving car sees? There's no one behind the wheel. So how does it know a child is about to cross?
On the roof, a spinning lidar fires millions of laser pulses every second, and times how long each one takes to bounce back.
Every echo becomes a dot. Together they build a live 3D map of everything around the car.
Cameras add color. They read traffic lights, signs and lane lines, which lasers can't.
Radar sees through rain and fog, and measures exactly how fast things are moving.
Software fuses all three into one picture. That's a car, that's a cyclist, that's a person.
Then it predicts where each one might go in the next few seconds, and plans a safe path around them. Many times every second.
Not everyone agrees on the recipe. Waymo uses lidar, cameras and radar. Tesla bets on cameras alone.
Either way, it never blinks, and never looks at its phone.
